findings.issue_text: [BUG] The forEach callback is changed to `async` and now contains `await getCalendar(...)`, but Array.prototype.forEach discards the returned promise, so the deletions run detached from the enclosing `try` block that this code sits inside. When rescheduling a booking whose references include a `_calendar` ref, any error thrown by `getCalendar` (e.g. a rejected dynamic import) or `calendar.deleteEvent` escapes the surrounding `try { ... } catch` that previously covered this body synchronously, becoming an unhandled promise rejection, and the reschedule flow proceeds (and the request resolves) as if the old calendar event was cleaned up when it was not.

[BUG] Identical defect to the vital copy: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` detaches the awaited work from the enclosing `try` block. On the reschedule path for wipemycalother bookings with calendar references, failures in `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` are no longer caught by the surrounding try/catch and surface as unhandled rejections, while the caller continues as though cleanup succeeded, leaving stale calendar events behind.

[BUG] The reschedule mutation's `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {` is changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` with `await getCalendar` inside, so the calendar deletions are not awaited by the tRPC handler and their rejections are unobserved. The reschedule endpoint returns its response before the old calendar events are deleted, and a failed `deleteEvent` (rejected import or API error) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of an error surfaced to the caller, so users see a successful reschedule while the old external event remains on their calendar.

[BUG] The diff converts every value of the shared `appStore` default export from a module namespace to a `Promise<module>`, changing the export's contract, but it only adds `await` at the call sites visible in this diff, leaving the prerequisite "every consumer of appStore must now await" unverified for the rest of the repository. Any consumer of `appStore[...]` not touched by this diff (the index is imported across packages/lib, packages/core, and the trpc routers) receives a Promise where it previously got a namespace object; the ubiquitous guard pattern `if (app && "lib" in app && ...)` is always false for a Promise (the `"lib" in promise` check never matches module exports), so the affected app is silently treated as "not implemented"/uninstalled and its feature no-ops with only a console.warn, rather than failing loudly.

[ADVISORY] The rewrite of the legacy cancel path from `forEach` to a `for...of` loop with `await getCalendar(credential)` serializes calendar-event deletions that previously were all issued concurrently before being collected into `apiDeletes`. A user cancelling a booking that has references on multiple calendar providers now waits for each provider's `getCalendar` dynamic import and `deleteEvent` round-trip one after another on the cancellation request path; cancellation latency grows linearly with the number of connected calendars instead of being bounded by the slowest one.

[ADVISORY] The booking-reference deletion block now exists in three hand-maintained copies (vital/lib/reschedule.ts, wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, and trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx), and this diff had to apply the identical `await getCalendar` fix to each one independently. The next behavioral change to reference cleanup (the async/await migration being the live example — it had to be replicated in three files and the parallel-edit hazard is exactly why the bookings.tsx copy still carries the broken async-forEach pattern) must be synchronized across all three sites or they drift, with each drift producing a distinct silent cleanup bug in a different app's reschedule path.

[BUG] The forEach callback was made async only to await getCalendar, but forEach discards the returned promise, so a failed dynamic import rejects outside the surrounding try/catch. On any reschedule where the calendar app module fails to load (or getCalendar rejects for another reason), the rejection escapes the try/catch (which was the entire point of the surrounding try) and becomes an unhandled rejection that can terminate the Node process; additionally the outer Reschedule function now resolves before any calendar deletion is even initiated, since the import is async, so deletions that previously started synchronously within the handler now race with handler completion and can be silently dropped.

[BUG] Same async-callback-in-forEach conversion: the awaited getCalendar rejection is unhandled because forEach does not await async callbacks and the try/catch cannot observe the promise. A dynamic-import failure during reschedule produces an unhandled rejection (process crash on Node >=15 defaults) instead of being caught by the adjacent catch block, and the handler completes before the deleteEvent calls begin, breaking the error-handling contract this code previously had when getCalendar was synchronous.

[BUG] The reschedule mutation's bookingRef loop was converted to forEach(async ...) to await getCalendar, making the deletion work fire-and-forget inside a tRPC procedure. The mutation resolves and returns its response before any calendar deletion starts (getCalendar is now an async dynamic import), and any rejection from getCalendar is an unhandled promise rejection rather than an error surfaced to the caller or caught by any error handler in the router — the client is told the reschedule succeeded while old calendar events are never deleted, and a failing app import can crash the server process.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials silently changed its return shape: the calendar field of each returned item is now Promise<Calendar | null> instead of Calendar | null, and the only consumer updated in this diff is getConnectedCalendars in the same file. Any other importer of the exported getCalendarCredentials (out-of-tree or later call sites) receives a Promise where it expects a Calendar object and will silently pass that Promise through (e.g. truthy checks succeed, calendar.deleteEvent is undefined) rather than failing fast; the shape change is invisible at the export boundary because the type is inferred and the diff only patched the one in-file consumer with `await item.calendar`.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials now eagerly kicks off a dynamic import promise for every calendar credential with no guaranteed awaiter, converting what was a synchronous metadata listing into floating-promise work on every listing path. Every call to getCalendarCredentials (including paths that only need integration/credential metadata for UI listing) triggers module loads for all relevant calendar apps; if an app module has a load-time error, what was previously a boot-time failure now surfaces as an unhandled rejection at arbitrary request time on this path, since nothing attaches a catch until getConnectedCalendars awaits inside its try.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds `await getCalendar` inside a non-awaited forEach(async ...) in the recurring-event branch while the adjacent else-branch was correctly converted to a sequential for-of loop, leaving the two sibling branches with inconsistent deletion semantics. Recurring-event calendar deletions still run fire-and-forget: the handler proceeds (and eventually responds) before the awaited imports resolve, and a getCalendar rejection in this branch is an unhandled rejection rather than an error in apiDeletes — the exact defect the else-branch conversion two hunks below was written to eliminate, left unfixed in the branch that handles the harder case (many bookings, many credentials).

[ADVISORY] No test coverage exists anywhere in the diff for this cross-cutting sync-to-async refactor (scanned all changed files: no spec/**, test/**, *.spec.* or *.test.* entries are present), despite it touching booking cancellation, reschedule, payment deletion, and calendar deletion. The refactor's core invariant — that every appStore[key] and getCalendar consumer now awaits — is enforced by nothing but manual inspection, and the diff itself demonstrates the failure mode: three call sites were converted to `forEach(async ...)` instead of proper awaiting, and none of the touched flows (cancel booking, reschedule via trpc, deletePayment) would catch a regression via CI; a future missed await fails silently at runtime on the deletion/payment paths where silent failure means orphaned calendar events or unrefunded payments.

[BUG] The forEach callback was made async to accommodate the now-async getCalendar, but forEach does not await, so the enclosing try/catch no longer observes rejections from getCalendar's dynamic import. If the dynamic import of the calendar app module rejects (chunk load failure), the rejection escapes the surrounding try block as an unhandled promise rejection and the booking's calendar event deletion is silently skipped while the reschedule flow reports success. Before this change getCalendar could not reject, so this failure mode is newly introduced; the same diff demonstrates the correct pattern (for..of) in handleCancelBooking.ts.

[BUG] The forEach callback was made async to accommodate the now-async getCalendar, but forEach does not await, so the enclosing try/catch no longer observes rejections from getCalendar's dynamic import. A rejected dynamic import becomes an unhandled promise rejection, the calendar event deletion for the rescheduled booking is silently skipped, and the reschedule flow still reports success; before this change getCalendar could not reject so the try/catch invariant held.

[BUG] The reschedule mutation's forEach callback was made async, so getCalendar's dynamic-import rejection is no longer observable by the mutation handler and the returned deletion promise is still discarded. On a failed app-module load the calendar event is never deleted but the tRPC mutation resolves successfully, leaving an orphaned external calendar event with no error surfaced to the caller; the rejection surfaces only as an unhandled promise rejection in the server logs.

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar without await, silently changing the exported contract so the `calendar` field of every returned object is a Promise<Calendar | null> instead of Calendar | null, and the diff adapts only one consumer (getConnectedCalendars via `await item.calendar`). The invariant that `.calendar` on getCalendarCredentials results is a resolved calendar or null is no longer enforced; any other consumer of this exported function destructuring `.calendar` and calling e.g. `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` gets a Promise object and throws TypeError at runtime, and TypeScript only catches it if the consumer's types are precise — the half-finished signature migration leaks Promises into a public API surface.

[ADVISORY] All 28 `import()` expressions are invoked eagerly when the appStore object literal is evaluated, so the laziness this PR exists to create is not actually achieved — merely importing appStore still initiates fetching and evaluation of every app module at startup; only the synchrony changed. Whoever relies on this change to defer app-module loading gets no deferral: every app chunk is requested at appStore module-evaluation time just as before, so startup cost is unimproved beyond bundle splitting; actual laziness requires an accessor (getter-based map or a function returning the import promise) rather than a plain object of eagerly-created promises.

Every server process still pays the full startup cost of loading and evaluating all app-store packages (now split into 28 parallel chunk fetches, which adds overhead); the 'async import' intent is not realized — the only change is that module top-level failures that previously failed fast at boot now surface as per-request rejected promises at each await site.

The surrounding try/catch could previously catch errors thrown synchronously inside the callback; now any rejection in the await chain is invisible to it, and under Node's default unhandled-rejection behavior (throw since v15) a single failing app chunk load can crash the booking-reschedule server process instead of being logged and degraded.

Previously the appStore lookup was a synchronous static-import access that could not fail per-item; now one broken/missing chunk (e.g. after a deploy) rejects the whole availability fetch, degrading free-busy lookup for every calendar of the user instead of skipping the one failed integration.

A regression in the await/guard logic (e.g. an unawaited promise or a mis-keyed appStore lookup) would silently drop every video adapter, breaking meeting creation, update, deletion, and video availability for all video integrations at once — with the diff's only verification being that the code compiles.

A rejected dynamic import or a throw inside getCalendar (e.g. credential with a type that maps to a missing appStore key) is no longer caught by the surrounding try/catch — it becomes an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the serverless handler, and the reschedule flow proceeds/responds without waiting for calendar cleanup, so calendar events can be silently left undeleted.

Failed calendar deletion during reschedule surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of the previous synchronous throw caught by the try block, and the wipe-my-cal cleanup can be abandoned mid-flight when the handler returns, leaving orphaned calendar events with no error surfaced to the caller.

[BUG] The reschedule handler's `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` makes calendar deletion a floating promise that the router procedure does not await. The tRPC procedure can return its response before `calendar?.deleteEvent` resolves or rejects; on serverless runtimes the lambda may be frozen/terminated before deletion completes (orphaned calendar events), and any rejection from the awaited dynamic import escapes trpc's error mapping as an unhandled rejection instead of an error response to the client.

[BUG] The recurring-event credential loop `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... for (const updBooking of updatedBookings) ... })` now runs entirely detached because forEach drops the async callback's promise. The per-booking calendar updates inside the inner for-loop (booker updateEvent calls over updatedBookings) are no longer ordered with or awaited by the handler; if the API response resolves first the updates are silently dropped for that credential, and a failure in `await getCalendar(credential)` is an unhandled rejection with no caller-visible error.

[ADVISORY] The `import(...)` calls in the object literal execute eagerly at module evaluation, so all 28 app chunks are requested at startup — this refactor does not actually defer app loading, it only wraps already-started loads in promises. The apparent intent (async/lazy app loading) is not achieved: every consumer pays a one-time Promise indirection and the change forces ~15 call sites across the codebase to become async (the entire rest of this diff) for zero deferral benefit; if lazy loading was the goal, the design misses it, and if bundle-splitting was the goal, that was achievable without making getCalendar/getVideoAdapters/deleteMeeting async and infecting every caller.

[BUG] An await of the now-async getCalendar was added inside the pre-existing fire-and-forget async forEach callback, so getCalendar rejections are unhandled and the entire per-credential updateEvent loop runs detached from the handler. If the dynamic import for any calendar credential rejects during cancellation of a recurring booking, the error surfaces as an unhandled rejection outside the handler's error handling (process crash on Node >=15), and the sequence of updateEvent calls across the recurring instances is no longer ordered relative to the rest of the handler, so cancellation can complete with some recurring instances left pointing at the old event.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach() was changed to take an async callback, so the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent work inside it is fire-and-forget and its rejections are no longer caught by the surrounding try/catch. When getCalendar's dynamic-import await rejects during a reschedule, the rejection escapes the enclosing try block as an unhandled promise rejection (which terminates Node >=15 processes) instead of being handled by the catch; additionally the handler proceeds to respond before any calendar deletion completes, so on serverless the deleteEvent work can be dropped entirely and stale events remain on the user's calendar with no error surfaced.

[BUG] Same async-callback forEach as vital/lib/reschedule.ts: the awaited getCalendar inside the forEach is never awaited by the loop, so rejections bypass the surrounding try/catch. A rejection from getCalendar during reschedule becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the enclosing catch, and the reschedule response is returned before the calendar deletions run, allowing deletions to be silently skipped on serverless runtimes.

In this tRPC mutation, a failing getCalendar await produces an unhandled promise rejection rather than a handled error, and the mutation returns success before the calendar event deletions have been issued, so users can see a successful uncancel/reschedule while their calendar events were never deleted.

[BUG] The per-credential forEach in the recurring-booking branch was changed to an async callback, so the awaited getCalendar and the subsequent per-booking calendar updates run detached from the handler with no await and no error handling. If getCalendar or the calendar updateEvent calls inside this loop fail, the rejection is unhandled (the handler has already moved on), and the cancel-booking response can complete before the recurring-event calendar updates are issued — on serverless those updates are dropped, leaving deleted bookings still occupying calendar slots; the loop also shadows the outer `calendar` variable, making the two differently-typed `calendar` bindings (one awaited Calendar, one Promise) easy to confuse in future edits.

Any other consumer of the exported getCalendarCredentials (in-repo or out-of-tree) now receives a Promise where it previously received a Calendar|null; typed consumers fail at build time, but pass-through or loosely-typed consumers end up passing a Promise object to client payloads or calling calendar methods on it, producing runtime NoMethodError-style failures instead of calendar data.

The next maintainer fixing the fire-and-forget forEach (or changing getCalendar's signature again) must remember both copies; missing one produces divergent behavior between the two apps that no type check will surface, exactly as this diff already shipped the same defect twice.

[BUG] The new `await getCalendar(credential)` sits inside a pre-existing fire-and-forget async forEach, so a dynamic-import rejection here becomes an unhandled promise rejection that no code in the cancel flow observes. During recurring-event cancellation, a chunk-load/import failure for a calendar app crashes the request via unhandledRejection (or is silently dropped in environments with a different handler) and the remaining per-credential event updates in the loop body are skipped without any error reaching the caller.

Callers written against the old contract, e.g. getCachedResults' Promise.all over calendars, now fail the entire availability computation (empty busy times returned as error) on a single app's import failure, instead of degrading to just skipping that calendar as the warn/null path was designed to do.

If getCalendar or deleteMeeting rejects during a reschedule, the rejection escapes the try{} block entirely (the catch is now dead code for this path); in Node's default configuration the unhandledRejection crashes the API process, and when it doesn't crash, the reschedule handler has already returned success while the calendar/video deletion silently never happened.

A failing calendar delete during reschedule is invisible to the catch block and to the caller — the endpoint reports success while the wipe/delete work was dropped, and the stray rejection can take down the Node process (default unhandledRejection=throw in Node >=15).

If the calendar module promise or deleteEvent rejects, the tRPC mutation still resolves successfully (the callback's rejection is never awaited or caught) while the old booking's calendar entry is never deleted — the user sees a successful reschedule with a stale/duplicate calendar event, and the orphan rejection is unhandled.

[BUG] getCalendar was made awaitable inside an already-async forEach callback whose promise is discarded, converting a previously synchronous (catchable/tracked) call path into a floating promise that can reject unhandled. During recurring-booking cancellation, a failure in getCalendar or the per-booking updateEvent calls now surfaces only as an unhandledRejection (potentially crashing the process) and the cancel endpoint responds without knowing the calendar updates failed — the recurring instances keep their stale calendar events with no error anywhere.

[BUG] Each import() promise is created eagerly at module-load time and cached permanently in the appStore object, so a failed module load produces a rejection that is unhandled until first awaited and is then served from the permanently-rejected cached promise forever. A module that fails to load (e.g. a missing chunk in a serverless deploy) previously failed the build/startup loudly; now it instead triggers an unhandledRejection at startup while unawaited (Node >=15 kills the process), and if the process survives, every subsequent getCalendar/getVideoAdapters/payment lookup for that app awaits the same cached rejected promise and 500s on every request — booking availability, event creation, and cancellation all fail per-request with no retry mechanism.

goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
